tasks.title: Make _is_module_creating existence-aware so EDITs of already-wired modules aren't flagged missing_wiring_oracle
acceptance_criteria: _is_module_creating returns True only when at least one non-test .py path in files_touched does NOT already exist on disk (resolved against the repo root).
A task whose only non-test .py file already exists on disk is NOT flagged module-creating, so an EDIT of an already-wired module no longer requires a *_wired.py oracle.
A genuinely new (absent) .py path is STILL flagged module-creating; mixed existing+new still flagged; external/out-of-repo absent paths still flagged (fail-safe).
Pure-edit meta types and test_*/tests/ paths keep their existing early-exit behavior unchanged; isinstance tolerance unchanged.

tests/planner/test_module_creating_existing_edit.py and tests/planner/test_module_creating_existing_edit_wired.py turn GREEN; tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py stays GREEN; no planner-suite regressions.
Only the single existing top-level function _is_module_creating is re-emitted as a symbol patch; signature, caller validate_plan, _is_wiring_oracle, and the pure-edit type set are untouched.

spec.objective: Fix the validator over-trigger (HANDOFF §3): _is_module_creating (harness/planner/plan_validator.py:31) returns True for ANY task whose files_touched has a non-test .py and whose meta_task_type is not a pure-edit type, never checking whether the file already exists. As a result every harness_self_fix EDIT leaf of an already-existing, already-wired module is wrongly flagged missing_wiring_oracle unless its verification_command names a *_wired.py test. Make the function existence-aware: a non-test .py that already exists on disk is an edit (creates nothing) and must NOT make the task module-creating.
functional_requirements: Inside _is_module_creating, derive the repo root as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] (Path is already imported at module top; the file lives at <repo>/harness/planner/plan_validator.py).

For each non-test .py path in files_touched, resolve it against the repo root (join repo_root with the path) unless the path is already absolute, in which case treat it as-is with no repo-root join; return True only if that resolved file does NOT already exist on disk.

If ALL non-test .py paths in files_touched already exist on disk, return False (no module is being created); only return True when at least one such path is absent (fail-safe: absent, including external working_dir/out-of-repo builds, => still module-creating).
Preserve the existing pure-edit meta_task_type early exit, the test_*/tests/ path skip, and all isinstance tolerance exactly as today; do not change the function signature or any other symbol.
spec.interfaces: _is_module_creating(task: Any) -> bool — unchanged signature; returns True only when at least one non-test .py in files_touched does NOT already exist on disk (resolved against the repo root via Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; absolute paths used as-is).
edge_cases: (a) A task whose only non-test .py exists on disk (an EDIT of an already-wired module) is NOT flagged module-creating and needs no *_wired oracle.
(b) A task whose non-test .py is a genuinely new/absent path (e.g. nonexistent harness/newmod.py) is STILL flagged module-creating.
(c) A task mixing an existing non-test .py with a new/absent non-test .py is STILL flagged (one absent path is enough).
(d) Pure-edit meta_task_types remain exempt regardless of file existence; test_* and tests/ paths are still skipped; non-string / non-.py entries are tolerated via isinstance.
(e) An absolute files_touched path is checked as-is (no repo-root join); an out-of-repo / external working_dir path that does not exist on disk is still treated as module-creating (fail-safe).
non_goals: No integration test — the change is exercised by the existing planner pipeline; do not author or modify any tests (oracles pre-committed).
Do NOT change _is_module_creating's signature or its caller validate_plan (:164); do NOT thread a repo_root parameter through validate_plan (multiple call sites, out of scope).
Do NOT touch _is_wiring_oracle, the pure-edit type set, or any other symbol in the file; do NOT add new top-level symbols.
Do NOT weaken the rule for genuinely new files or external-repo paths (absent => still module-creating); do NOT emit whole-file or __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__.
spec.implementation_notes:
EMISSION: symbol patch — re-emit the single existing top-level function _is_module_creating with the existence check added; touch exactly ONE symbol; no whole-file emit, no __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__, no new top-level symbols. Replace the current loop body (which does `return True` on the first non-test .py) so that instead of returning True immediately it computes the on-disk path and returns True only when that path is missing: repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; for each candidate path, p = Path(path); resolved = p if p.is_absolute() else (repo_root / p); if not resolved.exists(): return True; after the loop return False. Keep the pure-edit-type early exit, the `not isinstance(path, str) or not path.endswith('.py')` skip, and the `'tests/' in path.replace('\\','/')` skip exactly as they are now. The pre-committed guard tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py uses a nonexistent harness/newmod.py, so its new-module cases must stay rejected; the new oracle tests/planner/test_module_creating_existing_edit.py asserts an existing module is exempt and must turn GREEN.

## tests/planner/test_module_creating_existing_edit.py
```python
"""RED oracle: _is_module_creating must not treat an EDIT of an EXISTING module as
module-creating (HANDOFF §3).

Contract for the validator-existing-edit leaf: a task whose non-test .py
files_touched ALL already exist on disk (resolved against the repo root) is an EDIT,
not a module creation, and must NOT be flagged `missing_wiring_oracle` when its
verification_command lacks a *_wired test. A task touching at least one non-test .py
that does NOT exist on disk is still module-creating (fail-safe: unknown/absent =>
creating, so external working_dir builds keep today's behavior).

We assert specifically on the presence/absence of the `missing_wiring_oracle` code so
the test is robust to any other unrelated violations the plan may carry.
"""
from harness.planner.plan_validator import validate_plan, _is_module_creating

EXISTING = "harness/planner/plan_normalizer.py"          # tracked, exists on disk
NEW = "harness/planner/zz_definitely_not_existing_module.py"   # does not exist


def _task(*, files, vcmd="python -m pytest tests/planner/test_plan_normalizer.py -q"):
    return {
        "task_id": "HSF_EDIT_1",
        "title": "edit an existing planner module",
        "meta_task_type": "harness_self_fix",
        "priority": 1,
        "dependencies": [],
        "files_touched": files,
        "acceptance_criteria": ["edit lands", "suite green"],
        "spec_author": "test",
        "estimated_complexity": "S",
        "verification_command": vcmd,
    }


def _codes(task):
    return {v.code for v in validate_plan({"plan_kind": "implementation", "tasks": [task]})}


def test_edit_of_existing_module_not_flagged():
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" not in _codes(_task(files=[EXISTING]))


def test_new_module_still_flagged():
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" in _codes(_task(files=[NEW]))


def test_mixed_new_and_existing_still_flagged():
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" in _codes(_task(files=[EXISTING, NEW]))


def test_is_module_creating_consults_disk():
    assert _is_module_creating(_task(files=[EXISTING])) is False
    assert _is_module_creating(_task(files=[NEW])) is True


def test_pure_edit_types_still_exempt_regardless_of_existence():
    t = _task(files=[NEW])
    t["meta_task_type"] = "refactor"
    assert _is_module_creating(t) is False

```

The edit target harness/planner/plan_validator.py is an existing module reached from

## tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py
```python
"""RED oracle for the plan-validation wiring requirement
(epic: wire_up_phase, leaf: wiring-oracle-plan-validation).

Contract: a leaf that creates a NEW module must declare a WIRING oracle, or
validate_plan emits a `missing_wiring_oracle` violation pre-spawn. A wiring oracle is
recognised by its verification_command naming a `*_wired` test (the convention the
classifier keys on). A module-creating leaf whose only test is an isolated unit test
(no `_wired` oracle) is rejected; one that declares a wiring oracle passes the check.

We assert specifically on the presence/absence of the `missing_wiring_oracle` code so
the test is robust to any other unrelated violations the plan may carry.
"""
from harness.planner.plan_validator import validate_plan


def _task(*, vcmd, files):
    return {
        "task_id": "WUP_PV_1",
        "title": "create a new module",
        "meta_task_type": "harness_plumbing",
        "priority": 1,
        "dependencies": [],
        "files_touched": files,
        "acceptance_criteria": ["module exists", "wired into a live importer"],
        "spec_author": "test",
        "estimated_complexity": "S",
        "verification_command": vcmd,
    }


def _plan(task):
    return {"plan_kind": "implementation", "tasks": [task]}


def _codes(violations):
    return {v.code for v in violations}


def test_new_module_without_wiring_oracle_is_rejected():
    task = _task(
        vcmd="python -m pytest tests/harness/test_newmod.py -q",   # isolated unit test only
        files=["harness/newmod.py"],
    )
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" in _codes(validate_plan(_plan(task)))


def test_new_module_with_wiring_oracle_passes_the_check():
    task = _task(
        vcmd="python -m pytest tests/harness/test_newmod_wired.py -q",  # declares a wiring oracle
        files=["harness/newmod.py"],
    )
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" not in _codes(validate_plan(_plan(task)))


def test_pure_edit_leaf_not_required_to_have_wiring_oracle():
    # Editing an existing module (no new .py created) does not trigger the requirement.
    task = _task(
        vcmd="python -m pytest tests/harness/test_orchestrator.py -q",
        files=["harness/orchestrator.py"],
    )
    task["meta_task_type"] = "refactor"
    assert "missing_wiring_oracle" not in _codes(validate_plan(_plan(task)))

```
